solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hard to fathom good man getting right into obloquy

indicators.note: into says the good man and right go inside the word for obloquy

parts.note: obloquy is verbal abuse
ST, short for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous man takes his place amid a torrent of public abuse, which is hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abstruse is obscure and difficult to understand, hard to get to the bottom of.

clue.text: Bishop with Catholic church in which men connect

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Roman, as in Roman Catholic
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A bishop with a Catholic church where men come together.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a close non-sexual friendship between two men, a relationship where they bond.

clue.text: Paintings to appear in learned book perhaps that's hard work

indicators.note: to appear in means the paintings are set inside the book

parts.note: a tome is a large, often scholarly book
oils are paintings done in oil paint

explanation.surface: Getting your paintings into a scholarly volume is laborious.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilsome describes something demanding great effort and labour.

clue.text: Take lead from large boss

indicators.note: take lead from means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: jumbo means extra large

explanation.surface: An instruction to follow the lead of a big boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like an employer but is the raised knob at a shield's centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded projection at the centre of a shield is both an umbo and a boss.

clue.text: Stone me — man beheaded outside!

indicators.note: outside means the beheaded man surrounds the word me
beheaded means the first letter is cut off the man's name

parts.note: Gerald is a man's name

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a decapitated man outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me' reads as an exclamation, but 'Stone' is the definition and 'me' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious gemstone.

clue.text: With yam and fertile ground, here one may trace roots

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken down and reassembled

explanation.surface: A gardener with yams in rich soil, tracing their roots.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogical chart shows ancestry, where you trace your family origins.

clue.text: Bachelor getting into beer with wealthy old dwarf

indicators.note: getting into means the bachelor goes inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a beer
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: An unmarried man getting stuck into the beer with a rich old dwarf.
explanation.walkthrough: Alberich is the dwarf in Wagner's Ring cycle who steals the Rhinegold.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure of Germanic legend and Wagnerian opera is a Nibelung, a dwarf.

clue.text: Smitten gay men date heartless Trojan hunk

indicators.note: smitten means struck, so the letters are knocked into a new order
heartless means the middle is removed, leaving the outer letters of date

explanation.surface: Lovestruck men court a handsome Trojan with no feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganymede was the beautiful Trojan youth carried off by Zeus to be cupbearer to the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth he was the most beautiful of mortals, a prince of Troy, so a handsome Trojan.

clue.text: I'm sorry copper in restaurant rendezvous with secretary

indicators.note: in puts the chemical symbol for copper inside the restaurant date

parts.note: a meeting at a restaurant is a meal out
CU is the chemical symbol for copper
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: Someone apologises after a policeman turns up at a restaurant date with a secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element, CU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is an admission of fault, literally 'my fault', used as an apology.

clue.text: Matey only accommodating one in taxi

indicators.note: accommodating means the word for only holds the rest within it

parts.note: sole means only

indicators.note: in places the numeral one inside the word for a taxi

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is only being friendly by making room for one more in the taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey is informal for friendly and outgoing, as a sociable person is.

clue.text: Bookless characters felt line should be banter

indicators.note: Bookless asks for the abbreviation for book, B, to be removed from the word before it

parts.note: Braille is a system of raised characters read by touch
RY, short for railway, is a line

explanation.surface: Without books, someone felt that a line of characters ought to be a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters felt' is a cryptic description of BRAILLE, read by touch; dropping B (book) leaves RAILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing or ridicule, which is banter.

clue.text: Instruct colleague in the vernacular

parts.note: to inform someone is to instruct or tell them
an ally is an associate or colleague

explanation.surface: An instruction to brief a coworker in plain everyday language.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in the vernacular means using everyday casual speech rather than formal language.

clue.text: Bone a fish discovered in tin?

indicators.note: discovered in means the a and fish are found inside the word for tin

parts.note: tin is an example of a metal, flagged by the question mark
a carp is a fish

explanation.surface: A bone, of a fish, found in a can.
explanation.definitionFit: The metacarpals are the five bones of the hand between the wrist and fingers.

clue.text: Message that was sent with passion

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A love letter dispatched in the heat of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram was a message transmitted by telegraph cable, hence the informal term for it.

clue.text: Under Scots mountain hate festering

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: festering means rotting or souring, so the letters of hate are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Below a Highland peak, hatred is festering.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath and under both mean lower down than something.

clue.text: Obscene flaw in such valued stock?

parts.note: blue means risqué or obscene, as in blue jokes
a chip is a small flaw or nick

explanation.surface: An indecent defect in highly prized shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares in large, reliable companies are said to be blue-chip, valued and safe.

clue.text: Well-ordered condition of the pure in spirit?

definitions.meaning: the state of being tidy and orderly
a spirit drunk undiluted, with no mixer, is served neat

explanation.surface: The tidiness of a saintly soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pure in spirit' echoes the Beatitudes, but here it means undiluted alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is the condition of being orderly, and undiluted liquor is described as neat.

clue.text: Conceited weaver revolutionary artist spots astride horse

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the artist's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: astride means the spots straddle the horse, sitting either side of it

parts.note: acne is an outbreak of spots
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A vain weaver, a radical painter, notices pimples on someone riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Arachne boasted she wove better than Athena and was turned into a spider.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical figure was a weaver whose arrogance in challenging a goddess led to her punishment.

clue.text: Powerful feller Bond consulted

parts.note: a chain is a bond or fetter
to see, past tense saw, someone is to consult them, as one sees a doctor

explanation.surface: A strong man consulted with James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' reads as a man (fellow) but is a tool for felling trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorised saw with cutting teeth on a chain cuts down trees: a strong tree feller.

clue.text: Rap performance overheard offers dark scene

indicators.note: overheard means the words are taken as they would be heard spoken

parts.note: a rap is a knock on a door; a turn is a performance, as by a music-hall act

explanation.surface: A hip-hop act eavesdropped on presents a gloomy scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rap' looks like music, but is a knock on the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a painting of a night scene, as in Whistler's works.

clue.text: Encouraged to have wickedly divine time

indicators.note: wickedly suggests mischief, so the letters of divine and time are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tempted to have a deliciously naughty good time.
explanation.definitionFit: To be invited is to be asked or urged to do something, so encouraged.

clue.text: River in countryside with source hidden

indicators.note: with source hidden means the first letter, the word's source, is removed

parts.note: rural describes the countryside

explanation.surface: A river flowing through countryside whose spring cannot be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural flows from the Ural Mountains of Russia into the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: Legal document that might be a trap?

definitions.meaning: a deed transferring the title of property from one owner to another
a vehicle for transport, of which a pony trap is one kind

explanation.surface: A contract that could be a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed of transfer is a conveyance in law, and a horse-drawn carriage like a trap is a means of transport.

clue.text: Works caught on — sure success one concludes

indicators.note: concludes says the numeral one comes at the very end

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a cert is a certainty, a sure success
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something caught on and a sure hit concludes the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Concertos are musical compositions, so they are works, plural of opus.

clue.text: Cricket side succeeded, showing staying power?

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the side behind the batsman's legs
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A cricket team won, showing endurance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea or story that has legs is one with lasting appeal, with stamina to run and run.

clue.text: Time to restore confidence having lost one small gem

indicators.note: having lost means one of the letters is taken out of the word for restoring confidence

parts.note: to reassure someone is to restore their confidence
S is the abbreviation for small, and only one of the two is lost

explanation.surface: Time to comfort someone who has lost a little jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gem' is used of a person: a real gem, a real treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious, much-valued person is called a gem or treasure, both terms of praise.

clue.text: Lag having arrived behind schedule holds us back

indicators.note: holds means the words for arrived and late wrap around the rest

parts.note: in means arrived, as a train that is in
late means behind schedule

indicators.note: back means the word us is read backwards

explanation.surface: A delay, having got in late, keeps us waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' looks like delay, but here it is the verb meaning to wrap pipes against the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag a boiler or pipe is to cover it with protective material that keeps heat in.

clue.text: Denied having eaten pig inside

indicators.note: inside means the pig is placed within the word for having eaten

parts.note: dined means having eaten a meal
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone denied having eaten pork indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge or deny any connection with something.
